subject.title: feat: update Companion-owned Gateway safely in place

question: Should routine Companion-owned Gateway updates require a complete VHD rollback copy, or should the product adopt the layered rollback model accepted in the review discussion?
rationale: This is a user-facing durability, disk-capacity, and recovery-policy choice. The contributor has agreed the current default is not appropriate, but selecting the routine rollback contract cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical patch decision.

options.title: Adopt layered rollback
options.body: Use staged package rollback and verified Gateway-state backup for ordinary updates, reserving VHD recovery for incompatible migrations or explicit user-requested protection.

options.title: Keep full VHD rollback
options.body: Retain byte-for-byte recovery for every update, but require an explicit product decision plus capacity preflight, visible storage cost, retention cleanup, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause the update feature
options.body: Defer the in-place update transaction until the supported rollback contract and storage budget are defined.

recommendation.title: Adopt layered rollback
recommendation.body: Use staged package rollback and verified Gateway-state backup for ordinary updates, reserving VHD recovery for incompatible migrations or explicit user-requested protection.

likelyOwner.reason: The reviewer raised the concrete operational constraint that the contributor accepted, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the remaining policy choice.
